title: Bind P104 transport-cost screens to proper endpoint arrivals
body:
PR2640 leaves the cost of complete helper histories open. This source-bound follow-up couples all seven crossing inequalities with PR2353's requirement for 208 source-dependent proper arrivals at target hyperplanes. A total-lifetime floor is valid but weaker: its optimizer uses 1079/8 unproductive 0-to-9 histories. Enforcing actual proper arrivals strengthens the transport bound by 1.339066098318 at the selected exponent and 7.979043055690 at p=98/99.

The package certifies both fractional positive-transport relaxations over all 256 compositions of nine at p=1, the selected complex exponent, and p=98/99. Exact primal/dual brackets are narrower than 1e-40; replay imports neither the optimizer nor predecessor executables. An integer profile of 137 (1,7,1) histories and 71 all-unit histories meets every cut with capacity 4681 and exactly 208 arrivals. These necessary constraints therefore do not exclude 208 lifetimes.

The objective omits compatible geometry/chronology, ADDs, native adapters, hosting/idle, precision/tape and the consumer. This is a cost-screen result, not an attainable correction circuit, complete supplier bill or new kappa. The 482 upper bound is imposed hypothetically. Selected sources and frozen predecessors are unchanged.

Validation: registered CPython 3.12.14 replay and seven optimized test groups pass on Windows; CPython 3.14.6 optimized tests also pass. Independent integer-power/history oracles, a phantom-arrival failure case, false primal/dual certificates, source/predecessor drift, typed receipt corruption and Git-free read-only export are covered. The selected binding baseline and whitespace checks pass. No hosted CI, native correction replay, selected cold replay or proof-assistant check is claimed.

```sh
python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-crossing-profile-screen
```

Base: canonical main b4560d9e7216f72b73c5aa940ac099c05e33ccf9, priority revision 5. Exact predecessor heads: PR2640 2a5b9d72371211eac1288b690bc2739a97132439; PR2353 2704eadf6b5205d4b965e9c6fc6dce28b89783cf. TASK.json records selection, fresh overlap, limits and the stopping decision. [Scoped claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2640#issuecomment-6197334537).

Credit Nick Petalas/PR2640/2604, kumagi/PR2353, Philippe Van Velzen's screen, ywz65/PR2614, and the retained P104 geometry/native lineage detailed in the README. Prepared for Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human or separate-agent review claimed.

Final live overlap: 843 open PRs and 1307 Discussion records with complete pagination, fetched 16:55/16:57 UTC. A [concurrent broader budget investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2245#discussioncomment-18953694) was posted after the entry snapshot. This submission is explicitly narrowed to the proper-arrival encoding and independent transport certificates; it neither reviews unpublished code nor claims another full channel/ideal-idle budget result. The earlier claim retains concurrent credit.
